name: nowcastDFM
what_it_holds: R package implementing the Bok et al. (2017, NY Fed) dynamic factor model methodology: dfm() (EM estimation with missing data), predict_dfm(), and gen_news() which quantifies how each new data release/revision moves the nowcast -- a direct 'news decomposition' tool. On CRAN.
why_useful: Alternative DFM toolkit to FRBNY's MATLAB code, in R, with an explicit feature for decomposing how each new weekly data point moves the nowcast -- useful if building a homegrown weekly ABNB-demand tracker (gap #17).
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
why_all: Alternative DFM toolkit to FRBNY's MATLAB code, in R, with an explicit feature for decomposing how each new weekly data point moves the nowcast -- useful if building a homegrown weekly ABNB-demand tracker (gap #17).

gen_news() is the specific mechanism for attributing a KPI-nowcast change to which input series moved -- useful for building an auditable ABNB nights/GBV nowcast that can explain revisions between alt-data updates, matching the pitch's point-in-time discipline.

name: FredFetch
what_it_holds: MATLAB package with fred.latest(series) and fred.vint(series, vintage_date) for pulling FRED/ALFRED data at a specific vintage date, including a 'pseudo-vintage' mode that simulates publication lag for series without full ALFRED vintage history, plus parallelized bulk downloads across many series/vintage dates.
why_useful: Same ALFRED vintage capability as fredapi but for MATLAB users, and notably adds simulated publication-delay handling for series that lack full vintage archives -- useful if the team needs point-in-time treatment of a FRED series ALFRED doesn't fully vintage.
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: Same ALFRED vintage capability as fredapi but for MATLAB users, and notably adds simulated publication-delay handling for series that lack full vintage archives -- useful if the team needs point-in-time treatment of a FRED series ALFRED doesn't fully vintage.

name: macro-dashboard (zero-cost US macro forecasting engine)
what_it_holds: Vintage-true backtesting harness pulling 84 FRED series + full ALFRED vintages (~3,800 API calls for a full backtest) + BLS CPI/employment + Yahoo Finance gold, with release-date filtering, real ALFRED vintages, and expanding (not full-sample) z-scores to close look-ahead leak channels; validated over 147 quarterly as-of dates since 1990, 695 scored points, 0 leaks. No data files are committed -- everything is pulled live via tools/backfill.py.
why_useful: This is close to a working template for exactly the 'vintage-aware backtest' methodology gap #17/#4 calls for -- release-date filtering + real vintages + expanding-window normalization is the standard fix for the leakage problems the repo's own backtests must avoid. Worth reading as a reference implementation, not as a data source (no committed data).
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: This is close to a working template for exactly the 'vintage-aware backtest' methodology gap #17/#4 calls for -- release-date filtering + real vintages + expanding-window normalization is the standard fix for the leakage problems the repo's own backtests must avoid. Worth reading as a reference implementation, not as a data source (no committed data).

name: cfpb_data_downloader
what_it_holds: Small Python tool that calls the CFPB's public Consumer Complaints Database Trends API and downloads complaint-trend data (by product, company, issue, date range) to local files - a one-command pull, no auth needed.
why_useful: Turns the live CFPB complaint database into a repeatable, scriptable pull we can run at each guide date going forward, so we can build our own point-in-time vintage register of BNPL/travel-refund complaint counts (mentions of Airbnb, Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay) rather than relying on someone else's stale snapshot.
time_coverage: whatever the live CFPB API currently serves (2011-present)
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: Turns the live CFPB complaint database into a repeatable, scriptable pull we can run at each guide date going forward, so we can build our own point-in-time vintage register of BNPL/travel-refund complaint counts (mentions of Airbnb, Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay) rather than relying on someone else's stale snapshot.

name: nesstarR
what_it_holds: R package to parse NESSTAR binary survey data containers (.Nesstar files), specifically noted for use with MoSPI India survey microdata and other national statistical offices' legacy formats. 1 star, updated Jun 2026.
why_useful: Unlocks reading India's MoSPI legacy survey microdata files (household consumption/expenditure surveys) that are otherwise in an opaque binary format — relevant to gap #7's India MOSPI target and broadly to any NESSTAR-format national stats office archive.
themes: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients
why_all: Unlocks reading India's MoSPI legacy survey microdata files (household consumption/expenditure surveys) that are otherwise in an opaque binary format — relevant to gap #7's India MOSPI target and broadly to any NESSTAR-format national stats office archive.
